title: Carrot and Gochujang Focaccia
changes_from_base: Carrot juice and gochujang in the dough, a ginger, garlic and spring onion oil, and carrot ribbons with sesame on top.
summary: A bright orange focaccia made with carrot juice and gochujang, topped with carrot ribbons in a ginger, garlic and spring onion oil.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.note: choose one with no alcohol (ethanol or spirit) in the ingredients

ingredients.item: spring onions, thinly sliced, white and green parts kept apart
medium carrots, peeled into long ribbons

steps.title: Ginger oil
steps.text: Warm the neutral oil with the ginger, garlic and spring onion whites over low heat 3-4 min, until soft and fragrant. Stir in the sesame oil and cool.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Whisk the gochujang into the warm carrot juice and water, then add the flour, yeast and spring onion greens and mix until no flour shows; the dough will be a soft orange. Rest 15 min, then work in the salt.

steps.title: Folds
steps.text: Fold every 30 min, four times in all, until the dough is elastic and puffy.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Spoon 2 tbsp of the ginger oil, without the solids, into the tin, add the dough, turn to coat and stretch it out. Cover and leave about 1 h, until risen.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Toss the carrot ribbons with 1 tbsp of the ginger oil, dimple the dough and pile the ribbons loosely on top. Spoon over the remaining oil and aromatics and sprinkle with sesame seeds and flaky salt.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 25-28 min, until the ribbons are tinged brown at the tips and the bread is deep orange-gold; the centre reads about 96 °C. Cool 15 min on a rack.

tips: Check the gochujang label: some brands contain alcohol, and most contain wheat and soya.
Peel the carrot ribbons thin so they char at the tips without drying out.
Strain the oil for the tin and save the aromatics for the top, as the solids burn on the base.
storage: Best on the day. Keep wrapped at room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge for up to 3 days, then reheat at 200 °C for 5 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
